rv.q: Sher's performance is also the magnetic centre of a play which, even if a little aware of its own cleverness, reminds us that the movies are a product of Yiddish culture, and that the eternal battles between art and commerce were played out in the shtetls over a century ago.
Great subject matter but the play -- and the production --- fail to rise to their own piquant occasion.

cn.t: Wright's cinematic love letter divides critics, with some praising its intelligence and appeal while others find it falls short of the playwright's usual standards.
